title: Mitigate emission-lag spikes from GC pauses in mixed-precision kernel path
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customers (one enterprise Dedicated tenant and two Hosted accounts) reported sudden increases in initial token emission latency (TTFT-like behaviour) and irregular tokens/sec drops across long-context requests after the runtime-1.21 roll that included a new mixed-precision kernel path for sparse attention. Symptoms: 80–300ms spikes for the first emitted token and intermittent throughput collapse on 8k+ context windows. The issue reproduces under high-concurrency multiplex workloads and appears correlated with GC-like pauses in the worker executor when a kernel switch occurs.
incident_summary: 2026-03-09: On-call received an escalation from a Dedicated customer experiencing 2x initial latency on multi-turn generation with a 32k context. Investigation confirmed reproducible emission lag under load on the new mixed-precision code path. Affected environments: Hosted (eu-west-1) and Dedicated pools with heterogeneous GPUs. Private customer reported similar traces in air-gapped VPC after upgrading to runtime-1.21.
root_cause: A race between the kernel-transition path for mixed-precision sparse attention and our worker memory reclamation routine causes a brief stop-the-world pause in the executor thread. When the mixed-precision kernels request a temporary scratch allocation, the reclamation code takes an exclusive lock and runs a deferred compaction which stalls the scheduler. Under multiplexed, long-context requests the stall effects the first-token emission and reduces tokens/sec for the following period until the KV cache hot-path is re-primed.
mitigation: 1) Roll back the mixed-precision sparse-attention kernel selection for the most-severe pools in Hosted and mark the runtime as 'degraded-kernel' for Dedicated customers. 2) Backport a hotfix that converts the reclamation compaction into a cooperative step that yields to the executor (runtime-1.21.3). 3) Deploy a temporary routing rule to divert long-context requests for impacted models to an older stable kernel variant. 4) Notify affected customers with ETA and temporary mitigation details.

notes: This regression surfaced only for requests that blended very long context windows with high multiplex concurrency and where the mixed-precision kernel path was selected. Shorter contexts and single-tenant workloads were mostly unaffected. The cooperative reclamation approach trades a tiny steady CPU overhead for avoidance of stop-the-world pauses — acceptable while we investigate a lock-free allocator optimization for the next major runtime release.
